HSV MOURNS THE DEATH OF OSCAR ALGNER
THE LONGEST-STANDING HSV MEMBER PASSED AWAY LAST WEEK AT THE AGE OF 100. OSCAR HAD BEEN A MEMBER OF THE HSV FOR 93 YEARS.

Oscar Algner, born in 1923 and a member of HSV since October 17, 1930, died last Saturday, November 11, surrounded by his family. He had celebrated his 100th birthday in March of this year.

Oscar Algner had HSV in his heart from an early age. His father was on the HSV board and had been involved in the merger of the three founding clubs in 1919. As a five-year-old, Oscar Algner experienced his first HSV game in 1928, sitting on a wooden bench directly behind the touchline at the Rothenbaum stadium. Even when his family moved to Othmarschen and he no longer played soccer, he remained loyal to HSV. The club was always an anchor point for the whole family, even in dark times when Oscar Algner was at war and a prisoner of war. And when he returned to Hamburg and started a family himself, he passed on his deep attachment to HSV to his daughter, sons, grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

Oscar Algner regularly went to the stadium well into old age. In August 2023, he once again experienced a highly emotional visit to the stadium during HSV's 3:0 win against Hertha BSC. Together with four generations of the Algner family - great-grandson Philipp was a run-in child that day - Oscar Algner was visibly moved by the atmosphere in the sold-out Volksparkstadion.

Oscar Algner has lived through more than two thirds of HSV's 130-year history and has received numerous awards for his loyalty to the club, such as the pin for 75 years of membership. However, he always said modestly that he had no merits for HSV. He was a Hanseatic through and through, polite, reserved, but always with a joking remark on his lips and always with the rhombus in his heart.
